sections.overview: The Cuban Lizard-Cuckoo is a large island cuckoo; its close Caribbean lizard-cuckoo relative C. vieilloti is endemic to Puerto Rico.
sections.identification: It is a large, long-tailed bird with olive-brown upperparts and a conspicuous red eye-skin.
sections.habitat: On Cuba it occurs widely in wooded and forested habitats.
sections.diet: Its prey includes lizards and other small vertebrates, as well as insects.
sections.behavior: The Cuban account records it throughout the year, rather than as a seasonal migrant.
sections.reproduction: The references used here do not establish nest timing or clutch details for this species.
sections.ecology: Like C. vieilloti, it belongs to the Caribbean lizard-cuckoo group formerly placed in Saurothera.
sections.conservation: BirdLife treats the Cuban taxon as Least Concern; Bahamian birds have been split as C. bahamensis in some taxonomies.
